name: Cognition AI
monetization: Sells Devin, an autonomous AI software engineer, plus the Windsurf IDE — priced per-agent/per-seat to enterprises replacing or augmenting engineering capacity.
description_md: Cognition AI, founded in 2023, builds Devin — the first widely deployed autonomous 'AI software engineer' that plans, writes, tests, and ships code — and owns the Windsurf IDE after acquiring its product and team in July 2025 following Google's ~$2.4B license-hire of Windsurf's leadership. It raised $1B+ at a $26B valuation in May 2026 (co-led by Lux, General Catalyst, 8VC, with Founders Fund), and by August 2026 was reportedly already in talks to raise at $40B with revenue run-rate approaching $1B.
ai_monetization_md: Enterprise contracts for Devin agents (consumption/agent-hours) plus Windsurf subscriptions. Run-rate revenue climbed from $37M (May 2025) to $492M (May 2026), with management targeting >$1B later in 2026 — a figure TechCrunch reported the company was already approaching by August. The pitch is labor-substitution economics rather than tool economics: Devin is sold against the cost of an engineer, not the cost of an editor seat, and Cognition claims ~89–90% of its own committed code is Devin-written.
ai_strategy_md: Go straight at autonomous engineering rather than assistive coding: agents that own tickets end-to-end, with Windsurf as the human-in-the-loop surface acquired opportunistically when Google took only Windsurf's leadership. Aggressive capital velocity is itself strategy — valuation doubled ~8 months to $26B (May 2026), with $40B talks three months later — using each round to fund compute and enterprise land-grab before Anysphere/Copilot/Claude Code close the autonomy gap.
risk_notes_md: The reported ~$1B run-rate and the $40B raise talks are each single-sourced (TechCrunch, Aug 12, 2026) and unconfirmed — the $40B is talks, not a closed round. Competitive position is squeezed between Cursor's distribution (~$4B ARR) and frontier labs' own coding agents; like all coding startups it pays its model suppliers (who are also competitors). Revenue quality untested: agent-consumption contracts are young, and no retention/margin data is public.
